 At 5:03 p.m. on the eve of the midterm elections today, Hinds County Circuit Clerk Zack Wallace texted from 601-236-9373 to registered voters in one of Mississippi’s most populous counties a reminder that the polls are open Tuesday from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. The link went to a dead blue screen (above). The circuit clerk’s website has been down since at least Oct. 20, 2026, and the Hinds County Election Commission phone number has been disconnected since at least Oct. 21. Screenshot Hinds County website 
 JACKSON, Miss.—At 5:03 p.m. on the eve of the midterm elections today, Hinds County Circuit Clerk Zack Wallace texted from 601-236-9373 to registered voters in one of Mississippi’s most populous counties a reminder that the polls are open Tuesday from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. “For voter information and polling locations, visit https://www.hindscountyms.com/elected-offices/circuit-clerk ,” the text read. But that link is non-functional, opening instead to a blue screen with a small box in the middle reading: “U.S. NeXt: Website Coming Soon.” 
 Local Mississippi Officials Have Made 138 Polling Place Changes Ahead of the 2026 Election 
 Local election officials in Mississippi have made changes to 138 polling places since the 2024 election, including moving the location for 111 precincts, closing 22 precincts and opening five new precincts.

 This means that voters in Mississippi’s capital city of Jackson, which is 82% Black, are unable to access the county’s linked voter information page on the eve of Election Day. 
 The website has been down since at least Oct. 20, 2026, and the Hinds County Election Commission phone number has been disconnected since at least Oct. 21.
 The Mississippi Free Press informed Hinds County on Oct. 20 that its website was, at the time, redirecting to a website belonging to a local mental health clinic. Later that same day, the website began taking browsers to a 404 error page; it now shows the “website coming soon” notice.
The Mississippi Free Press tried to call the Hinds County Circuit Clerk’s office about the faulty text link and the blue screen, but could not reach them. The phone rang for about two minutes before hanging itself up at 6:10 p.m. An attempt to call the Hinds County Board of Supervisors office at 5:34 p.m. yielded the same results. 
 Hinds County residents can view all verified poll locations in the MFP’s fact-checked Trusted Elections precinct mapping tool , as well as view a list of poll location changes in Hinds County.

 Capital Bureau Reporter Grace E. Marion is covering the capital city, Jackson, as well as surrounding rural, urban and suburban areas in Hinds County, Madison County and Rankin County. She is a reporter and photojournalist with a passion for narrative writing and investigative reporting. Her work as a journalist has earned her coverage in publications like the Columbia Journalism Review, the Hechinger Report, and the Student Press Law Center. Grace is a member of the Investigative Reporters & Editors (IRE) and the Society of Professional Journalists (SPJ).
 Grace graduated from the University of Mississippi School of Journalism and New Media in 2022 with a degree in print and broadcast journalism, and from the University of California at Berkeley’s Graduate School of Journalism in 2024.
